title: Toy Train Tracks
solution_outline: P1: Interpret a track as a simple lattice cycle and construct it as the boundary of a row-convex polyomino. P2: Use a repeatable outward cross-bud rather than a long diagonal staircase: attaching four squares beyond a unique leftmost cell adds exactly eight curves and no straights, and preserves an attachment point. P3: A different positive-straight construction uses a horizontal backbone with alternating upward and downward teeth, rather than a diagonal staircase or repeated cross-buds. P4: Round both inventories down to even counts, using the stronger all-curved restriction when no straights remain.

nodes.name: Tracks are simple lattice cycles
nodes.statement: Joining centers of consecutive occupied track cells gives a simple unit-edge square-lattice cycle. A straight segment is a collinear vertex and a curve is a left or right quarter-turn; conversely such a cycle specifies a valid track.
nodes.accept: Identifies track cells with distinct lattice vertices, including the closing edge. Boundary vertices of an auxiliary lattice polygon can therefore be used as track cells; auxiliary polygon faces are not track pieces.

nodes.name: Both available counts round down evenly
nodes.statement: Every valid loop uses an even number of curves and an even number of straights. Its signed number of quarter-turns is four or minus four, and its total length is even by lattice bipartiteness.
nodes.accept: Uses L-R=±4 to deduce even L+R, and parity of a closed square-grid walk to deduce even total length and hence even straight count.

nodes.name: Restrictions on entirely curved loops
nodes.statement: A loop with no straights has length divisible by four, and cannot have length eight. Thus its length is either four or a multiple of four at least twelve.
nodes.accept: Axes alternate, and both axis-edge counts are even. For length eight, both bounding-box dimensions are at most two. A simple lattice polygon inside a 2-by-2 box with perimeter eight encloses either three cells in an L or all four cells; both boundaries contain straight vertices.

nodes.name: Staircase realizes all positive even straights
nodes.statement: For even C≥4 and even S≥2, take C/2 unit squares along a path alternating east and north. Extend the first square westward by (S-2)/2 additional squares. The union's simple boundary has exactly C turns and S collinear vertices.
nodes.accept: The staircase initially has perimeter C+2 and exactly two collinear boundary vertices, including the two-square base case. Adding the westward tail lengthens two exposed horizontal runs, adding two straight vertices per square and no turns. Consecutive rows overlap and the union has no holes or boundary self-touching.

nodes.name: Diagonal bands realize all-curved lengths
nodes.statement: For k≥1, occupy row y by cells x=y-1,y,y+1 for 0≤y<k, and add cells (0,-1) and (k-1,k). Its boundary is simple, turns at every vertex, and has length 4k+8. One square separately realizes length four.
nodes.accept: Consecutive three-cell rows shift right by one, overlap in two cells, and have singleton tips. Tracing either boundary side shows alternating horizontal and vertical edges; the perimeter is 4k+8. This covers precisely the claimed lengths at least twelve.

nodes.name: Trace an optimal staircase or band
nodes.statement: Let S=2⌊s/2⌋ and C=2⌊c/2⌋. If S≥2, output the staircase boundary with counts S,C. Otherwise output the band with the largest length divisible by four not exceeding c, replacing eight by four and using one square for four. Encode boundary vertices as S,L,R.
nodes.accept: This attains the independent parity upper bounds when S≥2 and the all-curved upper bound otherwise. A boundary of rows [l_y,r_y] is traced along the bottom, rising right outline, top, and descending left outline; cyclic changes of edge directions produce the output. O(s+c) time and space suffice.

nodes.name: Outward cross-bud adds eight curves
nodes.statement: For a polyomino with simple boundary and unique leftmost cell (a,b), add cells (a-1,b), (a-2,b), (a-1,b-1), (a-1,b+1). Its boundary stays simple, gains eight curves and no straights, and has unique leftmost cell (a-2,b).
nodes.accept: The exposed west edge is replaced by a nine-edge alternating path. Its two endpoint turns reverse handedness but remain turns, and its eight new vertices are turns. All new cells lie outside the previous bounding box, with no unwanted touching; the new left tip supports repetition.

nodes.name: Grow optimal loops from residue seeds
nodes.statement: Start with a staircase having the target straights and 4–10 curves matching the target modulo eight. For all-curved targets, use a 12- or 16-curve band, or a square for four. Apply cross-buds to reach the parity-bounded maximum counts, then output boundary turns.
nodes.accept: Targets are S=2 floor(s/2), C=2 floor(c/2) when S≥2; otherwise the largest multiple of four ≤c, replacing eight by four. Positive-straight seeds have 4,6,8,10 curves. Each seed has a unique leftmost cell. An occupied-cell hash table identifies exposed edges, which form one directed boundary cycle; encoding its cyclic turns takes expected O(s+c) time and O(s+c) space.

nodes.name: Staggered comb realizes positive straight counts
nodes.statement: For even C≥6 and even S≥2, set w=⌈C/4⌉. Occupy (x,0) and (x,(-1)^(x+1)) for 0≤x<w, omitting (0,-1) when C≡2 modulo four. Extend tooth (1,1) upward by (S-2)/2 cells. The simple boundary has C curves and S straights.
nodes.accept: The backbone and alternating teeth form a hole-free polyomino without boundary self-touching. Before extending a tooth, its perimeter is C+2 and exactly two vertices are collinear, as seen from the two end profiles. The isolated top tooth can be extended arbitrarily, adding two straight vertices per added square without changing turns.

nodes.name: Trace an optimal staggered comb
nodes.statement: Round s and c down to even counts. With positive usable straights, output the corresponding staggered comb, using a rectangle when the curve target is four. Otherwise output the largest all-curved band permitted by the divisibility and eight-curve restrictions, or a square for length four.
nodes.accept: The comb or rectangle uses S=2 floor(s/2) straights and C=2 floor(c/2) curves. Without usable straights, choose 4 floor(c/4), replacing eight by four. Store each column's bottom and top occupied cells; traverse the lower profile, right side, upper profile, and left side, encoding cyclic direction changes. O(s+c) time and space.

nodes.name: Opposed staircases realize positive straight counts
nodes.statement: Opposed monotone staircase chains joined by axial runs form simple loops with any positive even straight count and any even curve count at least four. Balanced chains realize curve counts divisible by four; offset chains realize the other even counts. Adjusting the axial runs supplies the straights.
nodes.accept: For target S,C, in movement notation use N^a W(SW)^q S^a E(NE)^q when C≡0 modulo four, with a=S/2+1,q=(C−4)/4; otherwise use N²(WN)^p W^b(SE)^{p+1} S E^{b−1}, with b=S/2+1,p=(C−6)/4. Each walk closes; separated monotone sides and end profiles prevent revisits. Cyclic direction comparisons give exactly S straights and C curves. Rotations, reflections, or equivalent chain descriptions count.

nodes.name: Encode an optimal opposed-staircase walk
nodes.statement: After rounding both budgets down to even counts, output the appropriate opposed-staircase loop when straights remain. Otherwise output the longest permitted diagonal band or square. Convert cyclic consecutive movement directions into S, L, and R.
nodes.accept: Choose N11 for positive usable straights. Otherwise use four curves for c<12 and 4⌊c/4⌋ curves otherwise. N5 can be emitted as (NE)²(SE)^k(SW)²(NW)^k, k=used_curves/4−2, or a four-edge square. Equal consecutive directions yield S; signed quarter-turns yield L/R, including wraparound. N2 and N3 prove maximality. O(s+c) time and space suffice.

end.statement: A solver holding every node of one END route can write a correct, fast enough program by routine coding; each route is an approach whose program the judge accepted.

hazards.statement: The output is cyclic: the turn between the last traversal edge and the first also contributes one segment, and no extra segment may be appended for closing the loop.
hazards.check: Inspect that exactly one character is emitted per polygon vertex, including the wraparound direction pair; the start vertex is not emitted twice.

hazards.statement: Availability limits apply separately to straights and curves; unused odd pieces are allowed. With zero or one available straight, eight curves alone cannot form a valid loop.
hazards.check: Check both segment-count limits and the all-curved small cases, especially c from eight through eleven. Ensure no division or unsigned underflow creates a negative staircase-tail length.

paths.approach: Interpret a track as a simple lattice cycle and construct it as the boundary of a row-convex polyomino. Both segment counts must be even; when fewer than two straights are available, alternating horizontal and vertical edges additionally force the curve count to be divisible by four, with eight impossible. Thin staircase polyominoes realize every even curve count with any positive even straight count, while diagonal bands with single-cell tips realize every all-curved length divisible by four from twelve onward; tracing their boundaries takes linear time.

Use a repeatable outward cross-bud rather than a long diagonal staircase: attaching four squares beyond a unique leftmost cell adds exactly eight curves and no straights, and preserves an attachment point. Choose one of four small staircase seeds when straights are available, or a twelve-/sixteen-curve seed otherwise, and repeat the bud until the optimal parity-bounded count is reached. Hashing occupied squares and tracing their exposed directed edges constructs the output in expected linear time.

A different positive-straight construction uses a horizontal backbone with alternating upward and downward teeth, rather than a diagonal staircase or repeated cross-buds. The staggered comb has exactly two straights and either 4w or 4w-2 curves; elongating one tooth supplies any additional even straight count. Together with the existing all-curved band construction and parity bounds, this gives an optimal loop, whose upper and lower profiles can be traced directly in linear time.

Round both inventories down to even counts, using the stronger all-curved restriction when no straights remain. With positive usable straights, construct one of two opposed-staircase walks according to the curve count modulo four, adjusting its axial runs to use all usable straights; otherwise use a diagonal band or square. These constructions attain the corresponding upper bounds, and encoding cyclic movement-direction changes takes O(s+c) time and space.
paths.notes: The reference's all-curves family is N5 up to a grid symmetry, with k=used_curves/4−2. Its positive-straight families adjust separation between opposed staircase sides rather than extending N4's terminal tail, so N6 does not cover this construction. N3 supplies the divisibility-by-four restriction omitted from the editorial's Lemma 3.

exploration.reason: Three distinct linear-time construction families have been accepted: diagonal staircases and bands, repeatable outward cross-buds, and staggered combs. No further complete approach with genuinely new intermediate claims is established.
considered: Direct formulas using repeated L/R substrings would encode the same boundaries already constructed, so they are implementation variants rather than new paths.
Exhaustive search or dynamic programming over self-avoiding lattice walks cannot handle up to 200,000 available pieces within the time limit.
Rectangles with separated independent protrusions consume too many straights when the straight budget is small; the useful alternating versions are already covered by the comb and cross-bud paths.

Local corner-removal surgery on all-curved bands can realize some additional count combinations, but does not uniformly cover the small cases and does not currently provide a separate complete construction family.

advisories: N2 (bundles claims a solver can have separately; split it): A solver can establish even curve count without establishing even straight count, which additionally uses the parity of the cycle length. Split these two parity claims, keeping the signed-turn and bipartiteness arguments as supporting evidence.

N3 (bundles claims a solver can have separately; split it): Divisibility by four and impossibility of length eight are distinct obstructions: the former leaves eight entirely unresolved. Split them so a solver who proves divisibility but gets stuck on the exceptional case can be located accurately.

N11 (bundles claims a solver can have separately; split it): The balanced and offset staircase families are separate construction insights; finding the family for curves divisible by four does not supply the other even residue class. Split the two families into construction nodes feeding N12.

order: For finer stuck-point localization, split N2 into curve parity and straight parity, split N3 into all-curved divisibility and the eight-curve obstruction, and split N11 into its two residue-class constructions. Retain the existing output-rule keys.
